_meta.comment: Shared data for the EcoMeter extension and the Legerly pricing page. 'api' = per-token USD (input/output). 'subscriptions' = consumer plan $/month. 'free_tiers' = which models each platform's FREE plan exposes (drives the extension model picker). To update prices, edit the numbers here.
_meta.source: Official provider pricing pages + free-tier availability
_meta.verified: 2026-08-24 against platform.claude.com/docs/en/about-claude/pricing, developers.openai.com/docs/pricing, ai.google.dev/gemini-api/docs/pricing, docs.x.ai/docs/models, api-docs.deepseek.com/quick_start/pricing, mistral.ai/pricing, docs.perplexity.ai/getting-started/pricing, plus the consumer plan pages openai.com/chatgpt/pricing, claude.com/pricing, gemini.google/subscriptions and x.ai/pricing. FOUR providers had moved since 2026-08-02. OpenAI cut gpt-5.6-sol $5/$30 -> $4/$20 (long $10/$45 -> $8/$30). Google put 3.6 Flash and the new 3.7 Flash on a half-price promotional rate through 2026-12-31. DeepSeek's warned increase LANDED: v4-flash and v4-pro are now 3x-4.5x their previous rates and are metered peak/off-peak by clock time. Anthropic made Sonnet 5's introductory $2/$10 permanent. xAI shipped Grok 4.6 and a new SuperGrok Plus tier. Mistral, Perplexity and Microsoft were unchanged. THEN 2026-08-29: three Chinese labs added — Alibaba (Qwen), Z.ai (GLM) and Moonshot (Kimi), eight models, read from their own rate cards that day; see _open_weights, _hosted_spread, _alibaba_tiering and _china_first_party_only below. The existing rates were not re-verified in that pass and still date from 2026-08-24.

caveats.claude-sonnet-5: $2/$10 per 1M is now the STANDARD rate. It launched as an introductory rate through 2026-08-31, and Anthropic's pricing page states the scheduled 2026-09-01 rise to $3/$15 will not occur. Resolved 2026-08-24 — no action needed at the end of August.
caveats._long_context: 'input'/'output' are the SHORT-CONTEXT rates. Where a provider charges more past a context threshold, the optional 'long' block holds { over, input, output }: 'over' is the INPUT-token count at which the higher rate starts, and that rate then applies to ALL tokens in the request, not just the excess. Thresholds are OpenAI >272k (per the tooltip on developers.openai.com/docs/pricing), Google >200k, xAI >=200k. Anthropic does not tier this way and has no 'long' block. A consumer that ignores 'long' silently undercounts long conversations by roughly 2x — which is the OPPOSITE direction to the unmodelled prompt-caching discount, so the two do not cancel out.
caveats._perplexity_request_fees: Sonar token rates are correct but they are not the whole bill. Perplexity also charges $5-$14 per 1,000 requests depending on model and search-context size. For chat-shaped usage that per-request fee typically exceeds the token cost, so any Perplexity figure derived from this file is a substantial UNDERCOUNT.
caveats._claude_tokenizer: Anthropic states that Claude 4.7 and later (Opus 4.7/4.8/5, Sonnet 5, Fable 5, Mythos 5) use a newer tokenizer producing approximately 30% more tokens for the same text than Sonnet 4.6 and earlier. Identical text is therefore NOT an identical token count across providers or across Claude generations. Any cross-model cost comparison built on a fixed token count understates these models by roughly a third.
caveats._legacy_keys: grok-4 / grok-3 / grok-3-mini, deepseek-v3 / deepseek-r1, mistral-medium-3 / mistral-small-3 and the o1 / gpt-4 / gpt-4-turbo family are no longer listed on their providers' current pricing pages. They are retained at last-known rates because they remain selectable in the extension's model picker; treat those numbers as historical, not current.
caveats._deepseek_increase_landed: The increase DeepSeek warned about has HAPPENED, found 2026-08-24. v4-flash went $0.14/$0.28 -> $0.44/$1.32 and v4-pro $0.435/$0.87 -> $1.32/$3.96 (peak rates): roughly 3x on input and 4.5x on output. DeepSeek is still the cheapest provider tracked, but by a far narrower margin, and the Auditor's downgrade advice leaned on the old numbers hardest.
caveats._deepseek_peak_offpeak: DeepSeek now meters by CLOCK TIME, which no other provider here does. Peak hours are 01:00-04:00 and 06:00-10:00 UTC Monday-Friday; every other hour is off-peak at half price. The rates stored above are the PEAK (undiscounted) rates, deliberately: off-peak is a discount you only get if your usage happens to fall outside a window you do not control, and quoting the cheap rate would understate the cost of the exact advice this project is most likely to give — 'drop your paid plan and pay per token'. Off-peak is exactly half of every figure stored.
caveats._promotional_rates: Some rates above are time-limited promotions, not standing prices, and they carry a machine-readable 'promo' block: { until, standard: { input, output } }. scripts/check-prices.js fails once 'until' is in the past, so an expired promo cannot quietly become a wrong price the way it nearly did with Sonnet 5. Currently: gemini-3.7-flash and gemini-3.6-flash are half price through 2026-12-31, reverting to $1.50/$7.50. Record the standard rate at the time you record the promo — going back to find it after expiry is how this data rots.
caveats._anthropic_fast_mode: Anthropic added a Fast mode (research preview) billing Opus 5 / Opus 4.8 at $10/$50 per 1M instead of $5/$25. Not modelled: it is an opt-in API service tier, like batch or caching, not the default rate a consumer pays. OpenAI renamed its equivalent 'priority' tier to 'Fast mode' on 2026-07-30; also not modelled.
caveats.deepseek-reasoner: DeepSeek's API aliases (deepseek-chat, deepseek-reasoner) track whichever model is current rather than a fixed version. Priced here as v4-flash and v4-pro respectively, which is an inference from DeepSeek's current lineup, not a published mapping.
caveats._open_weights: An 'open_weights' block means the weights are published and we have loaded the page they are on: { license, osi, params, url }. 'osi' is true only for a standard OSI-approved licence (Apache-2.0, MIT); it is FALSE for the bespoke licences the flagships carry, which are named after the model and must be read before use. Open weights is a property of a MODEL, not of a provider — Alibaba publishes weights for qwen3.8-27b and qwen3.8-2.4t-a95b but not for the qwen3.8-max and qwen3.8-flash tiers it sells alongside them, and Alibaba's own pricing page draws that line itself under a heading reading 'Text generation - Qwen (open source)'. Never badge a provider; badge the model.
caveats._hosted_spread: Where a model's weights are public, anyone can serve it, so the same model has many prices. The 'hosted' block records that spread as observed on OpenRouter on 'checked': n hosts, the cheapest and dearest, and how many undercut the model's own maker. 'input'/'output' remain the FIRST-PARTY list rate read from the lab's own page — the spread is context, not a replacement. TWO THINGS MAKE THIS LESS THAN LIKE-FOR-LIKE. (1) Hosts serve at different numeric precisions ('quant': int4, fp4, fp8, bf16, mxfp4). A 4-bit quantisation is a lossy compression of the weights, so the cheapest host is often not running the same computation as the dearest — the spread is partly a quality difference, not purely a margin difference. Most hosts do not state precision on their own pricing pages. (2) A host may list several SKUs for one model; we take the cheapest per host, so kimi-k2.7-code's first-party figure is the standard SKU, not the 'highspeed' one at double. Treat the range as indicative of a market, not as a like-for-like quote.
caveats._alibaba_tiering: Alibaba meters by INPUT-TOKEN COUNT with the tier rate applied to the whole request — the same semantics as the 'long' block above. All four models tracked here sit in a single 0-1M tier, so none carries a 'long' block, but other Qwen models on the same page have two or three tiers and would need one. Alibaba also prices the same model differently by region: qwen3.8-max is $2/$6 on the International tier and $1.65/$4.95 on Global. The International rate is stored, because that is the tab the page opens on and it matches the rate Alibaba charges through OpenRouter. One exception found: Alibaba's own OpenRouter listing for qwen3.8-27b is $0.425/$2.55, BELOW its published list price of $0.50/$3.00.
caveats._china_first_party_only: These three labs are priced from their own rate cards, read 2026-08-29: Alibaba Model Studio (alibabacloud.com/help/en/model-studio/model-pricing, JS-rendered — a plain fetch returns a shell with no prices), docs.z.ai/guides/overview/pricing, and platform.moonshot.ai/docs/pricing/{chat-k3,chat-k27-code}. Moonshot's docs serve a Markdown variant at the same path plus '.md', which is the reliable way to read them; three different pricing URLs there return a byte-identical SPA fallback if you guess the path.

anthropic.label: Claude
anthropic.note: Free plan: Sonnet 5 default (Sonnet 4.6 still selectable), limited Haiku 4.5. No Opus, Fable, or Mythos.

openai.label: ChatGPT
openai.note: Free plan: unlimited text chats on GPT-5.6 Luna (subject to abuse guardrails), plus Thinking Mini. GPT-5.5 has now FINISHED leaving the free tier — openai.com/chatgpt/pricing files it under "Legacy models" (Free: No, Go: No) and the Free Tier FAQ, updated 2026-08-13, lists only Luna. On 2026-08-08 that rollout was still in progress; it has completed. Free and Go get NO GPT-5.6 Sol at any reasoning level, and Terra only inside Work/Codex on desktop. Verified 2026-08-24.

google.label: Gemini
google.note: Free app: Gemini 3.6 Flash default, varying access to Gemini 3.1 Pro. Verified 2026-08-24 on gemini.google/subscriptions.

xai.label: Grok
xai.note: Free app runs Grok 4.6 — x.ai/pricing ticks Grok 4.6 in every column including Free, so xAI gates on rate limits, not model access. Verified 2026-08-24.

mistral.label: Mistral (Le Chat)
mistral.note: Free plan: Medium 3.5 and Small 4, ~25 messages/day.

perplexity.label: Perplexity
perplexity.note: Free plan: default Sonar, plus a ~$5/1k per-request search fee not shown here.

deepseek.label: DeepSeek
deepseek.note: Free web chat exposes the full model line-up (fair-use throttling only).

microsoft.label: Copilot
microsoft.note: Copilot resells OpenAI, but Microsoft publishes no model mapping for any consumer tier. Priced against GPT-5.5 as a stand-in only — not a disclosed mapping, and no API-equivalent cost is quoted for Copilot anywhere in the product.
